claims.text:
dagger-correction

**Identity / target / source:** `ai:dagger-correction` → `ai-dagger-correction` → `src/demos/ai/ai-dagger-correction`; source `company/domains/proposals/2026-10-18-ai-map-expansion.json#concepts/114`; brief `company/domains/briefs/2026-10-19-ai-next30e.md#13-dagger-correction`. **Packet:** R2. **Level / prerequisites:** stretch; `ai:behaviour-cloning-drift`.

**Nearest / distinct payoff:** behaviour-cloning-drift exposes unsupported states; this actually queries expert labels on visited states and refits a dataset lookup.

**Computed primary model:** Use the preceding3-step lane world; extend lanes to−1,0,+1. Expert actionAdvance at lane0, Correct otherwise. Original training data only center states. A rollout with forcedRight first visits(1,1),(2,1); query expert gives Correct labels at both. Aggregate them with original data; exact lookup fit now takesCorrect at(1,1) on a rerun, returns center at t2 and succeeds by t3.

**Countercase / boundary:** Repeating the original center demonstrations adds no off-lane state and does not repair the slipped rollout. An unqueried forcedLeft reaches lane−1 states and still fails under the updated lookup; another query/aggregation round is needed. Expert labels must be available and correct; no universal sample bound is inferred.

**Prediction / transfer recall:** Predict which extra labelled state changes the next slipped rollout; recall why right-lane corrections do not automatically label unseen left-lane states.

**Intervention / retained witness:** Collect learner states/Query expert/Refit lookup computes the actual aggregated table and changed rollout, with Repeat expert-only and Left slip contrasts. Retain before/after visited-state traces; no magic “improve policy” button without new labels.

**Source obligation:** [Ross–Gordon–Bagnell original DAgger PDF](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v15/ross11a/ross11a.pdf), opened2026-10-19, §2.1 expert-state supervision, §3 dataset aggregation/Algorithm3.1. The local finite state lookup/forced slip is not the paper’s driving benchmark or a claim of a universal recovery guarantee.
